limitations: One 60-second analysis window for corrected baseline and runtime/isolation controls; two repeats of current full profile. Descriptive sniff test, no release gate or full benchmark equivalence.
Historical long runs analyze replay seconds 60–420; these short runs analyze 30–90. Short source A/B does not resolve long-window historical drift.
Radar disable changes workload intentionally. It identifies current-profile cost, not a recently introduced Radar-code regression or an individual drawing primitive.
Electron runtime executable is varied; source trees retain their own installed build dependencies. Runtime control is same-current-source 45.3.2 versus 45.2.0.
Missing live/control/event/device paths remain as recorded by widget audit; no memory growth conclusion from these short runs.
Recorded foreground checks pass; no app UI switches, builds, tests or source edits issued during measured intervals.
conclusion: No aggregate current-source CPU increase was reproduced in the same-session short controls or later full-window pair. These limited comparisons do not establish statistical equivalence or clear pacing/memory gates. Source/runtime/dependency attribution remains partial.

definitions.cpu: Percent of total machine capacity; GPU process means CPU time, not GPU utilization.
definitions.analysis: Existing analyzer selects reporting intervals that overlap replay-play seconds 30?90, including an edge-crossing 5-second report bucket. It averages interval CPU samples without clipping them. Retained timeline includes each selected interval endpoint.
definitions.replay: Immediate post-play broadcast snapshot can still show pause; settled samples after 1 second must progress at 1x/session2/camera37/9/1.

limitations: One long old/current pair, not statistical equivalence or a full commit bisect. Other dependencies differ along with source; Electron-only control was performed earlier.
Historical cross-date CPU and renderer-pacing differences remain unexplained. No current-source aggregate CPU increase reproduced in this pair.
Both have poor overlay pacing. Current worst overlay-frame interval is 6088.5 ms; old worst is 633.8 ms. These are renderer timing observations, not game frame times.
Full workload gates remain inconclusive for missing event/channel/visibility conditions. No new PresentMon validation or production fix.
Old instrumentation reports zero-count Map measures from unused display windows; its raw animation rate cannot be compared with current rate without normalizing the reporting population.

reviewAudit.status: Same-session source controls did not reproduce an aggregate CPU/FPS regression. Historical cross-date drift, presentation cost, private growth, limited widget coverage and the rare overlay stall remain distinct findings. Neither canvas variant is retained.
reviewAudit.foregroundScope: iRacing was activated before capture and checked periodically through the UI. These point observations and the absence of other automated UI inputs support the intended foreground protocol; continuous OS foreground state was not recorded.
